newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Kohl says EU must make great efforts for EMU.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Kohl says EU must make great efforts for EMU.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday that Germany and other European Union member countries must still make great efforts to meet the economic entrance test for a single European currency.
Each nation should concentrate on getting its own affairs in order to meets the criteria for economic and monetary union (EMU) and worry less about the progress of others, he said.

While countries such as Spain and Italy have made great progress toward meeting the Maastricht targets for EMU, although they have further to go, Germany is coming precariously close to missing the deficit criteria this year.
But Germany will not veer from its position that the rules, which put ceilings on government deficits, debt, inflation and interest rates, should not be relaxed, Kohl said.
"We still have a lot to do to see that we fulfil the criteria, and I am strongly opposed to discussions that the criteria be changed," he said in a speech.

Under the Maastricht Treaty, countries hoping to participate in EMU should have deficits below three percent of gross domestic product (GDP). 1997 is the key year for deciding what countries will be in the first round of EMU, which is slated to start in January 1999.
Continued economic sluggishness and high unemployment forced Germany last month to revise its projection of this year's deficit upward to 2.9 percent of GDP.
But others should not take joy in Germany's difficulties, Kohl said. "We are seen as hard-working, and the hard-working are never well loved," Kohl said.
Bonn must work hard not just to meet the Maastricht criteria, but also to convince a sceptical public that the single currency, the euro, will be as solid against inflation as the mark, Kohl said.
"For Germans the deutschmark is not just any currency, it is the first currency in history that has brought us happiness."
The criteria for ensuring stability are not open to renegotiation and must be met, and the same goes for the EMU timetable, Kohl said.
